svg.text: Frame-based steganography · Fixed 400×400 · 127 bits · U-Net with hard mask · CNN Decoder + STN · Border-only encoding
Key: Message only modifies border pixels — center image preserved exactly
The encoder generates a residual for the entire image, but a hard binary mask PRESERVES the center pixels exactly.
Only the border frame region is modified. The decoder receives the full image + a border indicator channel.
Input: image (3×400×400) + mask (1×400×400) + message (127 bits) → Output: framed image (3×400×400)
⚠ conv10: Conv2d(32→32,3×3) computed but NOT used
Input: encoded image (3×400×400) + border mask (1×400×400) → Output: 127 logits
If no mask: border = ones(B,1,H,W) (full image)
Output: raw logits · sigmoid for training
1. 7-channel input: image(3) + binary mask(1) + message(3) — mask tells encoder WHERE to encode
2. SINGLE-channel residual: Conv2d(32→1, 1×1) expanded to RGB — forces uniform luminance change in border
3. Hard mask application: framed = img×mask + (img+residual)×(1-mask) — center pixels EXACTLY preserved
4. 4-channel decoder input: RGB(3) + border indicator(1) — tells decoder where to look for message
5. STN scale regularization loss prevents the STN from learning extreme zoom/rotation
6. Final concat is 71ch (vs 70ch in StegaStamp) due to 7ch input instead of 6ch
7. conv10 defined and computed but NOT used — residual takes conv9 output (same quirk as StegaStamp)
• Distortions applied to FULL image including frame region — decoder must be robust
• L2/LPIPS loss computed on BORDER region only (masked) — center has zero loss by design
• frame_width defaults to 8% of image size = 32px border on a 400×400 image
